gen-dafont-nordic-gf-marcellus-sc: Sparse, ancient, brushed onto paper: that is Nordic, with one flat stroke weight throughout. Marcellus SC is the serif beneath it, its curves thinning gently where they turn, and it is best left to big, short headings.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-montagu-slab: Weathered and stout, Nordic keeps its letters closed up tight like a folded leaf. Yet Montagu Slab opens the e wide and mixes sturdy downstrokes with slim turns, which is the real charm of the pairing.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-serif-hentaiga:
Nordic is the heading, powerful and ancient, with its letters pinched shut.

Noto Serif Hentaigana answers with open curves and subtle stroke modulation, and its small letters rise almost to capital height, so the stern top line and the softer text feel like two voices in one room.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-ovo:
Stencil-cut letters of one steady width mark Nordic at once.

Ovo, a classic serif, keeps its horizontals lighter but never threadlike, with shallow ascenders and a tall middle band, so paragraphs would move along with an authoritative, open-gapped ease.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-domine:
Domine takes the text, compact and dignified.

Beneath Nulshock's cable-like outlines, which never swell or thin, its moderate thickness changes and breathing curves would carry a long passage steadily, with sturdy tall lowercase keeping each line readable.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-esteban:
Nulshock stretches its spacious, unshaded outlines wide, each stroke as pipe-like and technical as a bent tube.

Esteban's understated variation and oversized lowercase make the strongest single draw.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-faustina:
Joins that refuse to thin out give Nulshock its bold, technical grip.

That is where it excels, while Faustina handles the quieter work, its bowls thinning gently and its open-jawed c keeping text approachable and authoritative.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-halant:
Nulshock sets a stretched, technical tone, its arches on r, n and m matching their stems exactly.

Halant then reads with a faint thick-thin shift and a towering x-height, so a longer stretch of text feels traditional and sturdy, with curves thickening gently at the shoulders.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-hedvig-letters-se:
Hedvig Letters Serif reads with sturdy, tall lowercase and open curves.

Nulshock's wire-like line glides above it, unshaded and spacious, while the body's mild thick-thin differences smooth the reading pace beneath, so the two feel deliberately unlike each other.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-lisu-bosa: Wide, wiry and technical, Nulshock gives every stroke the same visual weight in its heading. Yet Lisu Bosa lets its counters spill open and its sturdy lowercase flex gently, so a long passage would read with editorial, never dramatic, shifts in weight.
